UnitStatement: The analysis treats the governed agent instruction suite and governance documents as an engineered system.
The analysis traces systems engineering content to specific files, sections, and invariant IDs.
The architecture rests on ontology, epistemology, praxiology, and axiology as four philosophical pillars.
The four pillars are claimed to be architecturally generative for professional accountability in AI agent systems.
The systems engineering disciplines are claimed to be motivated by the four-pillar commitments in Chirality.
The analysis scope is limited to the instruction architecture, agent instruction files, governance documents, and binding contracts.
The method systematically analyzes eight systems engineering disciplines with evidence traced to files, sections, and invariant IDs.
The system enforces three distinct separations of concern.
The instruction root is physically separated from the working root.
Agents read instructions from one location and write project state to another location.
The instruction-versus-execution separation is stated in DIRECTIVE.md section 2.6 and enforced by runtime architecture.
Deliverable folders hold source truth and are structurally isolated from tool roots.
Tool roots contain agent-produced analysis and snapshots as derived outputs.
Human-accepted deliverable content is treated as source truth.
K-WRITE-1 enforces the source-truth boundary by requiring every agent to declare and stay within its write scope.
The Type 0/1/2 hierarchy separates standards definition, orchestration, and bounded task execution.
Authority flows downward from Type 0 through Type 1 to Type 2 agents.
Escalation flows upward from Type 2 through Type 1 to Type 0 or human gate authority.
The authority-versus-execution separation is enforced by agent instruction constraints and human gate authority.
The atomic unit of work is the production unit folder.
A production unit folder represents a single deliverable or knowledge type.
Each production unit folder is self-contained with identity, lifecycle state, dependencies, references, memory, and production documents.
K-HIER-1 enforces a flat package-to-deliverable hierarchy with no nesting.
K-WRITE-1 enforces deliverable-local agents writing only within their assigned folder.
The WORKING_ITEMS invariant prevents cross-deliverable scanning and editing by default.
Cross-deliverable operations are explicit opt-in operations.
Cross-deliverable operations write to isolated tool roots rather than deliverable folders.
Interfaces between agents are defined by identity, dependency, coordination, and brief mechanisms.
The _CONTEXT.md identity contract declares what a deliverable is, who owns it, and what it traces to.
Dependencies.csv v3.1 is a machine-readable dependency contract for typed edges between deliverables.
The _COORDINATION.md coordination contract defines project-level choreography semantics.
INIT-TASK briefs provide structured Type 2 agent inputs with validated enums.
Every interface is machine-checkable.
Every interface has explicit preconditions and postconditions.
Version control provides the development record for meaningful diffs, review, reproducibility, rollback, and audits.
A decision outside a versioned file does not exist for purposes of reliance.
All project state lives in git-tracked files.
The architecture uses no external database for project state.
Every state change produces a reviewable diff.
Every baseline is a git SHA.
Rollback is native through git revert or git reset.
The audit trail requires no special infrastructure.
K-AUTH-2 binds approvals to a specific git SHA.
Content changes after approval void the approval.
An approved deliverable is frozen at a specific commit.
Subsequent modification to an approved deliverable invalidates the approval and requires re-review.
K-VAL-1 marks a deliverable dirty when any governed input changes after its last approved SHA.
K-STALE-1 propagates upstream changes to all transitive dependent deliverables.
K-STALE-2 requires stale items to be triaged by a human before they are current.
Transitive change impact analysis marks downstream dependents stale when a deliverable changes.
Human triage resolves each stale item as no impact, needs rework, or needs review.
Staleness propagation prevents silent propagation of outdated assumptions.
K-SNAP-1 makes task-agent outputs to tool roots immutable snapshots.
Pointer files such as _LATEST.md may be overwritten.
Snapshot folders must not be overwritten.
Every analysis run produces a timestamped folder that is never modified.
Immutable snapshots create an append-only audit trail.
Pointer files provide convenience access to the most recent run without destroying history.
The immutable snapshot pattern is analogous to event sourcing in data engineering.
The system implements a V-model with decomposition down the left side and integration and verification up the right side.
AGENT_DECOMP_BASE.md defines a 7-gate decomposition protocol.
Phase 1 Intake captures source material and gates whether it reflects the source.
Phase 2 Normalize transforms source material into atomic units and vocabulary.
The Phase 2 gate asks whether units and classifications are correct.
Phase 3 Objectives derives success criteria and gates whether objectives represent success.
Phase 4 Partitions creates flat groupings with no overlap and no gaps.
The Phase 4 gate asks whether each unit is in exactly one partition.
Phase 5 Production Units operationalizes partitions.
The Phase 5 gate asks whether granularity and types are acceptable.
Phase 6 Coverage proves completeness and surfaces gaps.
The Phase 6 gate asks whether coverage and open issues are acceptable.
Phase 7 Publish finalizes the accepted decomposition.
The Phase 7 gate asks whether the decomposition is the accepted basis for downstream work.
Invariants I1 through I10 are maintained throughout decomposition.
Phase 6 produces machine-checkable Coverage and Telemetry metrics.
Coverage and Telemetry metrics make decomposition quality measurable across revisions.
AGENT_REVIEW.md implements a formal five-gate review process for lifecycle transitions.
Review Gate 1 checks lifecycle state and context validity.
At Review Gate 1, the agent validates and the human confirms scope.
Review Gate 2 generates checklists from specifications, decomposition, and dependencies.
At Review Gate 2, the agent derives checklist content and the human confirms completeness.
Review Gate 3 captures findings iteratively.
At Review Gate 3, the human provides findings and the agent records them with evidence.
Review Gate 4 performs disposition review.
At Review Gate 4, the human rules on all proposal findings.
Review Gate 5 makes the lifecycle transition decision.
At Review Gate 5, the agent recommends and the human approves.
IN_PROGRESS to CHECKING requires all critical findings to have non-TBD human disposition.
CHECKING to ISSUED requires all critical findings to be resolved.
CHECKING to ISSUED requires all major findings to be resolved or deferred with documented rationale.
The architecture uses decomposition coverage, dependency coverage, and review coverage.
Decomposition coverage maps every IN-scope atomic unit to exactly one partition.
Decomposition coverage maps every IN-scope atomic unit to at least one production unit.
Decomposition coverage records gaps as open issues with stable IDs.
Dependency coverage requires every active dependency row to have evidence.
Dependency evidence consists of EvidenceFile plus SourceRef.
Floating nodes without an IMPLEMENTS_NODE anchor generate warnings.
Review coverage derives checklists from acceptance criteria, objectives, consistency, dependency satisfaction, and TBD inventory.
Each review checklist item has a stable ID.
Traceability flows through scope traceability, requirement traceability, and provenance traceability.
Scope traceability requires every deliverable to trace to scope items, objectives, and the decomposition document.
TRACES_TO_REQUIREMENT rows connect deliverables to requirements, objectives, and scope items.
IMPLEMENTS_NODE rows connect deliverables to their parent package or WBS node.
Every extracted dependency row must cite evidence or explicit location TBD.
Every non-trivial claim in production documents requires a source citation or explicit epistemic label.
The Decomposition Ledger serves as the Requirements Traceability Matrix.
The Requirements Traceability Matrix maps every atomic unit through partitions to production units with objective linkage.
The write-scope architecture creates formal fault containment zones.
Deliverable-local agent failures are limited to one production unit folder.
Tool-root agent failures are limited to one tool root and leave source truth untouched.
Repo-level CHANGE actions require an explicit human approval token.
Read-only agents have zero write impact.
A Type 2 agent failure cannot corrupt source truth.
Type 2 agent writes are isolated to a tool root or single deliverable folder.
The CHANGE approval gate is the sole path from derived output to committed state.
The system makes failures explicit rather than preventing them.
Missing data is marked TBD and surfaced as an open issue through K-INVENT-1.
Conflicting sources produce a Conflict Table and require a human ruling through K-CONFLICT-1.
Invalid inputs produce FAILED_INPUTS and halt instead of guessing.
An unresolvable dependency target is represented as TargetType=UNKNOWN while preserving the raw reference.
Missing decomposition produces a warning and skips validation.
A lifecycle state violation warns rather than blocks because the human decides.
Failures are treated as visible findings instead of hidden recovery attempts.
Every uncertainty is labeled as FACT, ASSUMPTION, PROPOSAL, or TBD.
K-SEAL-1 prohibits Type 2 agent execution before context is sealed and gate-approved by a human.
K-GHOST-1 limits Type 2 agent context to folder contents plus declared references.
Context must be explicitly sealed before a specialist agent executes.
Declared references and deliverable folder contents define sealed context.
Context sealing prevents agents from operating on incomplete or undeclared context.
The decomposition protocol implements formal requirements decomposition.
The decomposition protocol transforms a source corpus into atomic units.
The decomposition protocol groups atomic units into flat partitions with no overlap and no gaps.
The decomposition protocol operationalizes partitions into production units with typed artifacts.
Allocation maps every IN-scope atomic unit to exactly one partition.
Allocation maps every IN-scope atomic unit to at least one production unit on a best-effort basis.
The Decomposition Ledger is the formal allocation record.
The system implements a requirements traceability matrix through three layers.
The Decomposition Ledger maps atomic units to partitions, production units, and objectives.
The Decomposition Ledger is machine-checkable.
The Decomposition Ledger requires UnitID, InOutStatus, PartitionID, ProductionUnitID(s), and ObjectiveID(s) columns.
Dependencies.csv ANCHOR rows provide the second requirements traceability matrix layer.
Each deliverable has exactly one IMPLEMENTS_NODE row tracing to its parent package.
TRACES_TO_REQUIREMENT rows trace deliverables to scope items, objectives, and requirements.
The _CONTEXT.md Scope Traceability section links each deliverable to source scope items and objectives.
_CONTEXT.md includes an explicit Acceptance Criteria section.
Acceptance criteria contain pass/fail conditions derived from the decomposition document.
PREPARATION creates acceptance criteria from decomposition metadata.
REVIEW verifies acceptance criteria at Gate 2 and Gate 5.
The system implements a closed-loop feedback control system across sessions.
The control loop begins with ORCHESTRATOR plant setup.
WORKING_ITEMS acts as an actuator that produces content.
TASK+dependency-extract rerun acts as a sensor that updates dependency state.
RECONCILIATION acts as a comparator that surfaces deviations.
CHANGE acts as output by committing to baseline.
ORCHESTRATOR scan acts as feedback by reporting new state.
Lifecycle state has ISSUED as set point, _STATUS.md as sensor, and REVIEW gate as actuator.
Dependency closure has all active dependencies satisfied as set point, Dependencies.csv as sensor, and RECONCILIATION as actuator.
Decomposition fidelity has zero unassigned units as set point, Decomposition Ledger as sensor, and human correction as actuator.
Work availability has no blocked deliverables as set point, blocker analysis as sensor, and tier sequencing as actuator.
Artifact completeness has all anticipated artifacts present as set point, folder scan as sensor, and WORKING_ITEMS as actuator.
In an open-loop session, WORKING_ITEMS produces content within a single deliverable without cross-deliverable feedback.
Open-loop work is bounded by deliverable scope and session objective.
Across sessions, NEXT_INSTANCE_STATE.md carries state between sessions.
After content changes, TASK+dependency-extract rerun updates the dependency graph.
RECONCILIATION detects integration defects across sessions.
ORCHESTRATOR scan computes work availability for the next tier.
The ORCHESTRATOR invariant states that human authority is the halting condition.
Every control-loop iteration requires human confirmation at gates.
The system cannot autonomously advance tiers.
The system cannot autonomously approve deliverables.
The system cannot autonomously resolve conflicts.
Human gates function as decision authority in the control loop.
The system proposes while the human decides whether to continue, hold, or redirect.
The architecture defines three layers of formally stated invariants.
I1 through I10 impose structural constraints on decomposition.
Decomposition constraints include flat partitions, no gaps, stable IDs, deterministic coupling, and vocabulary discipline.
Decomposition agents enforce I1 through I10.
AUDIT_DECOMP verifies I1 through I10.
R1 through R9 impose behavioral constraints on all agents.

R1 through R9 cover human decision rights, straight-through tasks, write quarantine, immutable snapshots, provenance, no invention, conflict surfacing, brief-driven execution, and hygienic publication.
Agent instructions enforce R1 through R9.
K-* invariants cover hierarchy, authority, sealing, dependencies, status, staleness, gates, merge, provenance, invention, conflicts, claim strength, write scope, and snapshots.
CONTRACT.md defines K-* invariants with enforcement points.
Each ORCHESTRATOR function has explicit preconditions and postconditions.
ORCHESTRATOR Initialize requires a decomposition document to exist.
ORCHESTRATOR Initialize produces _COORDINATION.md and records the coordination representation.
ORCHESTRATOR Scaffold requires Function 1 completion and tool roots to exist.
ORCHESTRATOR Scaffold initializes all deliverables and generates semantic artifacts.
ORCHESTRATOR Scan and Report requires deliverables to have _STATUS.md.
ORCHESTRATOR Scan and Report reports state and computes blockers when mode enables blockers.
ORCHESTRATOR Estimating requires BOE, INDEX.md, and price sources to exist.
ORCHESTRATOR Estimating produces estimation snapshots per tier.
ORCHESTRATOR Control Loop requires Function 1 to be complete.
ORCHESTRATOR Control Loop creates handoff artifacts and makes the ownership boundary clear.
Type 2 agents enforce preconditions as input validation.
Invalid Type 2 inputs produce FAILED_INPUTS and halt.
Missing optional data allows continuation with TBD marking and warnings.
The architecture defines a formal type system through enumerated domains.
The decomposition ontology includes AtomicUnit, Partition, ProductionUnit, and Objective.
AtomicUnit contains id, statement, status, and sourceRef fields.
AtomicUnit status is enumerated as IN, OUT, or TBD.
Partition contains id, name, scopeDesc, inclusions, and exclusions fields.
ProductionUnit contains id, name, parentPartition, type, responsible, and artifacts fields.
Objective contains id, statement, and mappedUnits fields.
DependencyClass is enumerated as ANCHOR or EXECUTION.
AnchorType is enumerated as IMPLEMENTS_NODE, TRACES_TO_REQUIREMENT, or NOT_APPLICABLE.
Direction is enumerated as UPSTREAM or DOWNSTREAM.
DependencyType is enumerated as PREREQUISITE, INTERFACE, HANDOVER, CONSTRAINT, ENABLES, or OTHER.
TargetType is enumerated as DELIVERABLE, PACKAGE, WBS_NODE, REQUIREMENT, DOCUMENT, EQUIPMENT, EXTERNAL, or UNKNOWN.
Confidence is enumerated as HIGH, MEDIUM, or LOW.
Origin is enumerated as DECLARED or EXTRACTED.
Explicitness is enumerated as EXPLICIT or IMPLICIT.
Status is enumerated as ACTIVE or RETIRED.
SatisfactionStatus is enumerated as TBD, PENDING, IN_PROGRESS, SATISFIED, WAIVED, or NOT_APPLICABLE.
ReviewType is enumerated as SELF_CHECK, PEER_REVIEW, IDC, or INDEPENDENT_VERIFICATION.
FindingSeverity is enumerated as CRITICAL, MAJOR, MINOR, or OBSERVATION.
FindingDisposition is enumerated as ACCEPT_AS_IS, REVISE, DEFER, NOT_APPLICABLE, or WITHDRAWN.
FindingStatus is enumerated as OPEN, RESOLVED, DEFERRED, or WITHDRAWN.
EpistemicLabel is enumerated as FACT, ASSUMPTION, PROPOSAL, or TBD.
The type domains constrain agent behavior through enum validation, schema checking, and conditional logic.
The deliverable lifecycle is a formal state machine with authorized transition actors.
The lifecycle path proceeds from OPEN to INITIALIZED to SEMANTIC_READY to IN_PROGRESS to CHECKING to ISSUED.
PREPARATION authorizes the OPEN to INITIALIZED transition.
TASK+four-documents or TASK+domain-documents authorizes the INITIALIZED to SEMANTIC_READY transition.
TASK+semantic-matrix-build authorizes the SEMANTIC_READY to IN_PROGRESS transition.
A human authorizes the IN_PROGRESS to CHECKING transition.
REVIEW plus human approval authorizes the CHECKING to ISSUED transition.
K-STATUS-1 makes _STATUS.md the canonical state indicator.
Lifecycle transitions are forward-only under normal operation.
Each lifecycle transition is recorded in append-only History with date, actor, and rationale.
The system explicitly separates human-owned decisions from agent-executable actions.
Humans own scope and boundary decisions.
Humans select governing codes, standards, and design basis.
Humans own hazard and risk acceptance.
Humans own conflict adjudication and rulings.
Humans own approval, issuance, and signature.
Agents may execute scaffolding and initialization.
Agents may execute bulk document drafting.
Agents may execute dependency extraction and register maintenance.
Agents may execute coverage analysis and reconciliation reporting.
Agents may execute estimation and scheduling as derived, non-authoritative work.
Agents may execute aggregation and collation.
K-AUTH-1 enforces that only humans author binding approval records.
K-BIND-1 enforces that approvals are always binding and only binding.
The architecture reduces cognitive load through epistemic transparency, conflict surfacing, memory externalization, vocabulary canonicalization, and flat hierarchy.
Every claim is labeled as FACT, ASSUMPTION, PROPOSAL, or TBD.
Epistemic labels let the human distinguish grounded values from inferred values.
K-INVENT-1 and K-CONFLICT-1 enforce epistemic transparency.
Contradictions are not resolved silently.
The Conflict Table pattern presents disagreements in a structured format for adjudication.
MEMORY.md externalizes per-deliverable working memory.
NEXT_INSTANCE_STATE.md externalizes per-session context between sessions.
Working memory is organized by semantic topic.
Every decomposition requires a Vocabulary Map.
The Vocabulary Map defines canonical terms and maps synonyms.
Vocabulary canonicalization prevents semantic drift across team members and sessions.
K-HIER-1 enforces a flat hierarchy that helps humans comprehend the full project structure.
K-GATE-1 makes gates dynamic per project instance.
The minimum required gates are seal transition and pipeline run approval.
Additional gates are project-configurable.
The human chooses the coordination representation.
Coordination representation values are SCHEDULE_FIRST, DECLARED, and FULL_GRAPH.
Dependency tracking mode scales among NOT_TRACKED, DECLARED, and FULL_GRAPH.
When dependency tracking is NOT_TRACKED, the system does not compute blockers.
Suppressing blocker computation in NOT_TRACKED mode avoids false precision.
The dependency model separates structural identity from execution coupling.
Tree ANCHOR rows connect deliverables to the definition hierarchy.
Each deliverable has exactly one IMPLEMENTS_NODE anchor.
The tree model is stable and normative.
The tree model defines what a deliverable is.
DAG EXECUTION rows capture information flow between deliverables.
The DAG model is many-to-many, current, and operative.
The DAG model defines what a deliverable needs.
The dual-graph model prevents scope drift while supporting dynamic execution planning.
K-DEP-1 makes deliverable-local _DEPENDENCIES.md and Dependencies.csv authoritative.
There is no central dependency graph.
Dependency aggregation is on-demand.
Each deliverable maintains its own dependency register.
Cross-deliverable views are produced on demand by read-only agents.
Cross-deliverable views are materialized as immutable snapshots in tool roots.
The dependency graph remains current because it is derived from files rather than copied into a database.
K-PROV-1, K-INVENT-1, and K-CONFLICT-1 function as a safety mechanism.
K-PROV-1 ensures every claim can be audited back to its source.
K-INVENT-1 ensures evidence gaps are visible instead of papered over.
K-CONFLICT-1 ensures disagreements reach the human decision-maker.
The epistemic controls address plausible unsupported LLM output by requiring provenance.
Unsupported claims become structurally visible through provenance requirements.
CONTRACT.md section 2 defines four enforcement layers.
Agent instructions constrain intent at design time.
The agent-instruction layer checks K-GHOST-1, K-WRITE-1, K-SNAP-1, K-PROV-1, K-INVENT-1, K-CONFLICT-1, K-DEP-1, and K-DEP-2.
ORCHESTRATOR checks K-SEAL-1, K-GATE-1, and K-HIER-1 during initialization and pipeline execution.
Human review checks authority, approval, binding, staleness, merge, validation, and status invariants at every gate decision.
Future tooling checks automated invariants continuously or on demand.
The multi-layer enforcement strategy ensures no single enforcement failure can compromise system integrity.
The systems engineering content of the architecture is not incidental.
Instruction files are formal specifications that define interfaces, state machines, invariants, preconditions, postconditions, containment zones, and authority boundaries.
DIRECTIVE.md, SPEC.md, TYPES.md, and CONTRACT.md form a coherent specification hierarchy.
The specification hierarchy runs from intent to physical structures to vocabulary to binding invariants.
Systems engineering disciplines are the mechanism by which agents coordinate.
Systems engineering disciplines are the means by which failures are contained.
Systems engineering disciplines are the basis on which humans maintain authority.
The Type 0/1/2 hierarchy adapts classical systems engineering patterns to governing LLM-based agents.
The write-scope architecture, invariant system, gate-controlled workflows, and evidence-first epistemology adapt classical systems engineering patterns to professional agent governance.
The eight systems engineering disciplines emerged as a way to operationalize the four-pillar commitments.
The eight systems engineering disciplines were not selected from a handbook and bolted onto the architecture.
A commitment to stable, inspectable git-tracked state motivated configuration management and baseline control.
A commitment to mandatory provenance and epistemic transparency motivated verification, validation, formal methods, and evidence-first patterns.
A commitment to bounded gate-controlled execution motivated safety engineering, control theory, and fault containment architecture.
A commitment to non-delegable professional responsibility motivated human factors design and decision authority allocation.
Ontology maps to architecture and structural design plus configuration management.
Epistemology maps to verification and validation, formal methods, and requirements traceability.
Praxiology maps to safety and reliability engineering plus control theory.
Axiology maps to human factors and decision authority allocation.
Each systems engineering discipline serves one or more pillars.
No systems engineering discipline was found that does not serve a pillar.
In Chirality, systems engineering disciplines formally express the philosophical commitments.
Systems engineering disciplines make the philosophical commitments architecturally real.
Systems engineering is the architecture's means of taking professional AI agent governance accountability seriously.
The four pillars strongly predict what kinds of systems engineering disciplines should be present.
The analysis confirms the four-pillar prediction within the Chirality implementation.
